arts.name: Principle of equalisation
u: The Confederation ensures financial equalisation between its States in order to guarantee real equality of opportunity among citizens and the balanced development of the confederal territory.
The purpose of equalisation is to reduce disparities in financial capacity between States without removing the incentives for sound budgetary management.
No State may be excluded from the equalisation scheme on grounds related to the dominant national affiliation of its population.

arts.name: Equalisation formula
u: Confederal law sets the equalisation formula according to the following principles:

equalisation is calculated from objective and publicly verifiable indicators: population, gross domestic product per inhabitant, fiscal capacity, and indicators of need (density, geography, socio-demographic burdens);
no State may, after equalisation, have tax resources per inhabitant below eighty-five per cent of the confederal average;
no contributing State may be deprived, by way of equalisation, of more than thirty per cent of the surplus of its fiscal capacity over the confederal average;
the equalisation formula is revised every six years, after review by the Ustavni Sud of its conformity with constitutional principles;
any amendment to the equalisation formula is subject to the mandatory consent of the Narodni Sabor under Article 109.

arts.name: Financial transparency
u: The confederal department of Finance and the Treasury publishes each year a public report detailing, State by State, the financial flows between the Confederation and the States: confederal revenue collected, allocations paid, equalisation received or contributed.

Certified by the Confederal Court of Audit (Article 136 bis), this report is transmitted to the Kongres, the Narodni Sabor and the Ustavni Sud. It is made public in the three regional standards within forty-five days of the close of the financial year.

Any State, any autonomous entity and any citizen may bring a complaint for breach of financial equality before the Ustavni Sud if they consider that the recorded flows depart without justification from the statutory formula.

arts.name: Principle of geographic proportionality
u: Confederal investment in transport, communications, energy and research infrastructure, and in cultural facilities of confederal interest, is distributed according to the principle of geographic proportionality.
No State may be durably excluded from the major confederal investment programmes.

arts.name: Multi-year programming
u: For each multi-year investment programme, confederal law sets distribution targets:
among the three regional standards (western, central, eastern), according to a key that takes account of demographic weight and established needs;
among the geographic areas of the Confederation, taking care not to concentrate investment in the most densely populated territories alone.
Any multi-year investment programme above a threshold set by law is submitted to the Narodni Sabor for an opinion before its adoption by the Kongres.

arts.name: Complaint for manifest disproportion
u: Any State that considers itself wronged by the distribution of a confederal investment programme may refer the matter to the Ustavni Sud.

The Ustavni Sud may annul any investment programme whose geographic distribution appears manifestly disproportionate with regard to real needs, constitutional indicators and earlier multi-year commitments.
In the event of annulment, the Konfederalno Veće has one hundred and twenty days to propose a revised programme.

arts.name: Confederal Court of Audit
u: The Confederal Court of Audit (Konfederalni Računski Sud) is the independent organ for the control of the finances of the Confederation.
audits the accounts and management of the Confederation, its administrations and the institutions it finances;
certifies the annual report on financial flows between the Confederation and the States (Article 133) and verifies the calculation of equalisation (Article 132);
audits the implementation of multi-year investment programmes (Articles 134 to 136).

It is composed of seven members, one per constituent people, elected by the Kongres from among three candidates proposed by each national delegation of the Narodni Sabor, by the majority laid down in Article 117, for a non-renewable term of nine years.
It addresses its reports to the Kongres and the Narodni Sabor and makes them public in the three regional standards.
